transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Patel (Redwood SE), Karen Holt (CISO, Westwood Bank), Rajiv Sharma (Head Cloud Eng), Marta Lee (IT Compliance)

Summary: Initial discovery focused on data residency requirements for Westwood's new LLM features. Customer is evaluating Redwood Hosted for speed, Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict data residency and KMS controls. Key concerns: EU data residency, logging/audit retention, HIPAA overlap for certain products, and proof of encryption key custody. Next: send security docs, schedule SE deep dive, provide pricing and trial.

00:00 Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery from Redwood, I work on the enterprise team. Miguel who is our SE is also on the call, we'll run through a few quick questions about your compliance needs and then dig into the deployment options.
00:22 Karen Holt: Thanks, Avery. I'll keep it short, we are evaluating LLM features for customer support automation and some internal knowledge base use. Primary ask is data residency — we need EU-hosted data for EU customers and strict controls around audit logs, retention, and access. Also concerned about HIPAA for a small subset of use cases.
00:40 Miguel Patel: Great, Karen. Can you describe your current infra footprint? Are you multi-cloud or primarily AWS?
00:48 Rajiv Sharma: We're hybrid — majority on AWS in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, some GCP for analytics. For any EU data we need full residency in eu-west-1 or a partner datacenter in Frankfurt. We also have strict egress rules — logs containing PII can't leave region.
01:10 Marta Lee: To add, our compliance team requires KMS-based key ownership for anything that could be PHI, and audit logs that are immutable for seven years for some financial records.
01:25 Avery Chen: Understood. High level on Redwood options: Hosted API is easiest and fastest to onboard, but for strict residency and key custody Dedicated or Private are the recommended routes. With Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools and region pinning; with Private you can run the control plane in your VPC or on-prem with customer-managed KMS.
01:44 Karen Holt: Quick question — if we go Hosted, do you offer EU-only tenancy or guarantee logs stay in EU?
01:50 Miguel Patel: Hosted can be region pinned and we offer EU-only hosting for accounts, but Hosted still has shared control plane elements and some metadata may be processed in our control plane. For absolute custody and the most restrictive policies we recommend Private where the control plane sits in your VPC. (small pause) sorry, "control plane" sometimes in notes gets turned into 'control plain' in transcriptions.
02:14 Rajiv Sharma: When you say control plane in our VPC, do you mean the entire Redwood stack or just the management plane?
02:20 Miguel Patel: The Private deployment option allows the control plane to be customer-managed; you can run the management endpoints in your VPC and we can integrate with your KMS/HSM. In some on-prem cases customers run the inference runtime and control plane fully inside their network — that's the most locked-down model.
02:40 Karen Holt: About logging — we need to redact or disable input logging for certain endpoints, and we need audit logs to be write-once. Does Redwood Support configurable logging retention and redaction?
02:53 Avery Chen: Yes, we have per-route logging policies; you can disable content logging, enable only metadata, or route logs to your logging stack via a VPC endpoint. Retention policies are configurable but Hosted has constraints; Dedicated lets you set longer retention windows and Private gives you full control to ship logs to your SIEM.
03:14 Marta Lee: HIPAA — some of our support transcripts include health-related info. Do you have HIPAA BAAs and attestation?
03:21 Miguel Patel: Redwood has HIPAA-compliant offerings for Dedicated and Private deployments. We can sign a BAA for Dedicated with appropriate controls; for Hosted we need to evaluate on a case-by-case basis. I'll follow up and send our HIPAA questionnaire and BAA docs.
03:38 Karen Holt: Encryption — we need to ensure keys never leave our vault. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys (BYOK) that never leave our KMS?
03:47 Miguel Patel: Yes, with Private you can generally keep full key custody. With Dedicated we support KMS integrations and can use customer keys in HSM; some tokenization/edge-talk may still be proxied. We'll need to walk through the exact key flow in the technical deep dive.
04:05 Rajiv Sharma: We like the idea of Dedicated because of reserved capacity and the SLA but concerned about bursting and cost. How does Redwood handle burst capacity and fallback?
04:15 Avery Chen: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and optional burst capacity. At high level, you can set burst to fallback to a lower-cost model or to Hosted failover. For compliance we can set policies that prevent routing outside the region or to public Hosted endpoints.
04:34 Karen Holt: Can you show us an example of audit logs and what fields are contained? We need to see immutability flags and retention controls.
04:43 Miguel Patel: I'll attach our log schema in the follow-up — it includes timestamps, request id, route, model variant, region, and optional redaction flags. Note that demo logs in Hosted may still include tokenized metadata in some cases; in Private we can ensure logs never leave your environment.
05:05 (brief crosstalk)
05:12 Karen Holt: Who at Redwood will be our point for compliance conversations? I want someone technical and someone legal.
05:18 Avery Chen: I'll be your AE and coordinate, Miguel is your SE. I'll also bring our compliance lead if needed to review contracts and BAAs.
05:30 Rajiv Sharma: Timeline — we are looking to decide by end of Q2, with a pilot starting mid-April if things look good. Any blockers?
05:38 Avery Chen: That timeline aligns. Typical blockers are benchmark results and contractual slas. We'll propose a short pilot in eu-west-1 using either Hosted EU tenancy or a Dedicated pool depending on your preference.
05:52 Marta Lee: A few nitty-gritty items: data minimization, right to be forgotten, GDPR DSAR processes — we need guarantees around the ability to delete user-level data on request.
06:08 Miguel Patel: For Dedicated/Private you can implement deletion at the storage layer. For Hosted, deletion is doable but requires coordination — some metadata persists for operational reasons. We'll include a DSAR playbook in the follow-up.
06:25 Karen Holt: Are there standard pen test reports and recent SOC2 certs we can review?
06:30 Avery Chen: Yes, I'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and recent pentest summary after redaction as part of the security packet.
06:37 Rajiv Sharma: From a technical perspective, we need to measure latency for our common prompt sizes. Do you have benchmark data for latency in Dedicated vs Hosted in eu-west-1?
06:47 Miguel Patel: We have perf profiles and model benchmarks. For small 256-token responses Dedicated can hit lower P99 latency due to reserved GPU pools and caching. I'll prepare a short benchmark spreadsheet with expected p50/p90/p99 for your workload.
07:05 Karen Holt: Back to key custody — we have a separate requirement: any PHI must be encrypted with customer keys and KMS audit trail must be integrated with our SIEM. Can Redwood push KMS audit events to our SIEM?
07:20 Miguel Patel: We can forward audit logs to your SIEM through a private peering or syslog endpoint in Private. For Dedicated we can also provide a log-forwarding option. We'll need network details.
07:35 (short pause)
07:40 Rajiv Sharma: One more — training data handling. We don't want Redwood to use our data for model training. How do you handle data usage policies?
07:50 Avery Chen: Redwood's enterprise contracts include clauses preventing customer data from being used to train public models. For Hosted there's a setting to opt out of data ingestion for training; Dedicated and Private give stronger guarantees because data doesn't leave your environment. We'll include contractual language in the follow up.
08:08 Karen Holt: Any known certifications for cloud partners in EU? We need to confirm provider compliance.
08:15 Miguel Patel: We publish our partner compliance matrix. I'll attach that, it maps our deployments to underlying cloud region compliance (AWS eu-west-1, Azure Germany regions, etc.).
08:28 Karen Holt: What about data residency for backups and snapshots? Those often move to other regions for redundancy.
08:35 Miguel Patel: Good point. For Dedicated and Private you can specify backup residency policies; for Hosted we have cross-region replication for resilience but we can restrict to EU-only replication for certain accounts. We'll need to validate for your backup SLAs.
08:53 Marta Lee: How about deletion of KV cache or prefixes — we need a guarantee that cached keys or conversation prefixes can be invalidated immediately.
09:03 Miguel Patel: We have APIs to purge KV cache and prefix caches. In Private you control the runtime so purge is immediate; in Hosted and Dedicated there can be short propagation delays. I'll document expected TTLs.
09:20 (notes and link mentions)
09:28 Avery Chen: I'm adding the follow-ups: 1) Security packet (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/pen test) 2) Log schema and DSAR playbook 3) Benchmark sheet for eu-west-1 4) Pricing for Dedicated and Private 5) Proposed pilot plan
09:45 Karen Holt: Sounds good. One small item on vendor risk — our procurement requires a signed DPA and proof of cyber insurance.
09:54 Avery Chen: We'll include a standard DPA and details on insurance limits; if you need higher limits we can escalate.
10:03 Rajiv Sharma: For the pilot, can we get a test account that restricts logging of transcripts and uses EU keys?
10:10 Miguel Patel: Yes, we can provision a pilot in eu-west-1 with logging disabled and with customer-managed keys, subject to contract. We'll outline steps in the next email.
10:22 Karen Holt: Okay, recap and owners?
10:26 Avery Chen: Recap: Redwood to send security packet, Miguel to prepare SE deep dive + benchmark plan, Westwood to share compliance checklist and network details. I'll schedule the deep dive for next week.
10:40 Marta Lee: Thanks all. Quick note, transcription quality on this call is fine but expect the auto transcript to mess with some proper nouns.
10:48 Avery Chen: Noted — we'll send clean docs. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
